strengths: Decision-ordered IA: summary answers plan/price/renewal/usage, compare toggle explicitly comparison-only, review names recurring price, effective date and next renewal.
Cancellation is discoverable via nav and danger section, primary safe exit Keep my plan, acknowledgement gate, scheduled state with Resume and member explanations replacing dead controls.

Strong error simulation and honest preview language: failNext for change/cancel/payment, expired-card validation, success banner with Preview only, no payment-success claims; checks confirm no overflow or console errors.

verdict: Candidate A is more disciplined on billing truth, tighter visual hierarchy and stronger verifiable states, with exact member-impact consequences and separate two-step cancellation. Candidate B has a clear decision-ordered IA, safe-exit cancellation and richer simulated failures, but its plan comparison adds unsupported feature content, its page duplicates billing facts into a much longer scroll, and its state evidence is almost entirely missing (only default skeletons). On comparable desktop and mobile full-page views, Candidate A better answers plan, price, renewal and limit at a glance in a trustworthy billing context.
limitations: One blinded judge pass from evidence packets only: no dialog or member/success renders were available, state screenshots for Candidate B and several Candidate A states show loading skeletons, and no live interaction or assistive-technology testing was performed; this is not a statistical test or proof of causation.
